Sampson Family Farm

NO Added Steroids, Hormones, Antibiotics or Animal by-Products
Certified GRASSFED and FINISHED Angus Beef and Katahdin Lamb

Sampson Family Farm is a three-generation family farm in Live Oak, Florida. Our livestock are pasture-raised using regenerative and sustainable practices that support healthy animals, healthy soil, and productive pastures.

Through rotational grazing, seasonal forage, and hay grown on our farm, we provide a natural, forage-based diet year-round. Our animals are raised without added hormones, steroids, animal by-products, or routine antibiotics and are handled using low-stress practices.

We are a true pasture-to-plate farm, offering bulk beef and lamb shares and USDA-inspected individual cuts directly to families who want to know where their food comes from and how it was raised.

We believe continued education is essential to positive growth.
We are always learning, adapting, and applying new knowledge to improve our farm, our livestock, and our land.

Our Farm Standards
From a Traditional Cattle Farm to Direct-to-Family Farming

Like many cattle producers, we originally raised calves for the conventional livestock market.

Over time, we began asking ourselves whether there was a better way to connect the care we put into raising our livestock with the food families were bringing to their tables.

We wanted greater control over how our animals were raised, what they ate, and how they were handled throughout their lives. Just as importantly, we wanted our customers to be able to know the farm and the people behind their food.

We started small, selling processed beef directly to families looking for naturally raised, high-quality meat. What began as a small part of our farm gradually became the heart of our operation.

In 2015, Sampson Family Farm became the first farm in Florida to earn Certified Grassfed by A Greener World for beef, followed by the same certification for our sheep in 2017.

Today, we raise Angus cattle and Katahdin sheep using a pasture-based, grass-fed and grass-finished production system.

Farming With the Land

We believe healthy livestock begins with healthy soil and healthy pastures.

Our cattle and sheep are managed through rotational grazing, moving between pastures throughout the year rather than remaining continuously in one area.

During the warmer months, they graze native grasses, improved pastures, wooded forage areas, and other naturally available vegetation. During the cooler months, we plant seasonal forage and cover crops and supplement grazing with hay produced on our own farm when needed.

Rotational grazing allows pastures time to rest and recover while helping distribute manure naturally, improve soil health, protect plant growth, and make better use of the land.

It also gives us greater control over what our livestock consume throughout the year.

Our goal has never been to produce the greatest number of animals possible. Our goal is to raise healthy livestock responsibly while continually improving the land that supports them.

Raising Food for Other Families

Today, we harvest approximately 80–90 grass-fed and grass-finished steers and about 30 lambs each year.

We intentionally remain a relatively small operation because personal livestock management is important to us. We want to know our animals, understand our pastures, and maintain the standards we have established over decades of farming.

Our beef and lamb are sold directly to customers through:

Bulk freezer shares
Individual USDA-inspected cuts
Farm pickup
Farmers markets
Florida Meat Up locations

For more than a decade, we have had the privilege of meeting many of the families who purchase food from our farm. Those relationships are an important part of why direct-to-consumer farming means so much to us.

Customers aren’t simply purchasing beef or lamb.

They have the opportunity to know where their food was raised, how the animals were managed, and who raised it.

Our Commitment to the Land and Livestock

We plan to continue improving our rotational grazing system, soil health, livestock handling facilities, and pasture management while maintaining the personal care that has always been part of our farm.

We believe responsible farming requires constant observation, learning, and improvement.

Every pasture is different. Every growing season is different. Weather, livestock needs, and environmental conditions change from year to year. Our responsibility is to adjust while continuing to protect the health of our animals and the land entrusted to us.

Our Promise

Trends in agriculture will change. Markets will change. Technology will change.

The principles behind Sampson Family Farm will not.

We will continue to focus on:

Family ownership and hands-on management
Grass-fed and grass-finished livestock
Responsible animal care
Pasture-based and rotational grazing
Healthy soil and long-term land stewardship
Transparency about how our animals are raised
Direct relationships with the families who purchase our food
Building a farm that can continue into the next generation

After more than 30 years of raising cattle, we are still learning, adapting, and improving.

We invite you to learn more about our family, our farming practices, and how we raise the beef and lamb that goes from our pastures to your family’s table.

— The Sampson Family

Question and Answer Page
Q: How do you raise your beef and lamb?
As natural as we can without giving up personal care that keeps our livestock and land healthy. During the summer months the entire herd; cows, calves and sheep are out on native grass and forage pastures. During the winter months the herd is grazing cover forage and supplemented with our own baled hay.
Q: What products do you have for sale?
We Raise Angus Cattle and Katahdin Meat Sheep.We only market livestock that are born and raised on our farm.We only use processors that are certified Animal Humane Approved Facility.You can purchase certified beef for your freezer by the Quarter, Half or Whole or by individual USDA cuts.You can purchase certified lamb for your freezer by Half or Whole or by individual USDA cuts.
Q: How do I get my meat?
When you are ready to reserve a steer/lamb and place your order a deposit is required.At harvest time we will deliver your steer/lamb to the AWA processor.Beef will hang in the cooler for 10-12 days, Lamb hang 1-2 days.Whole and Half orders will have the chance to create a custom cut list with the processor.Cuts are vacuum sealed and marked by processor.You can pick up directly from the processor, the farm or one of our Meat Up Locations around the state.
Q: How much meat can I expect from a beef purchase?
Whole, half or quarters under the custom exempt law are sold as live weight, determined by the processors certified scales.We prefer to process steers around 1000-1100 lbs. (final freezer weight will be around 400+ lbs.)Final freezer weight after processing will be approximately 25-30% less than the hanging weight due to shrinkage from hanging, boning, trimming, etc.
Q: What cuts come in my beef purchase?
When you order whole or half cow, you will have the ability to custom order your cuts.A quarter is a split half; each quarter receives equal parts of the half side from the front and back.An average quarter gives around 95 - 100 lbs: 35-40 packages chopped ground beef, chuck roasts, shoulder roasts, brisket, filets, New York strips, sirloin, ribeyes, soup bones and stew meat.
Q: How much freezer space and meat will my family need?
Approximately every 35 lbs. of meat will require 1 cubic ft.A quarter of beef usually fits in the freezer section of a conventional refrigerator if it is completely empty.A whole beef needs 10 cubic feet of freezer space.An average family of four will be content for a year with 1 whole beef.Vacuum-wrapped meat will keep well for 1 year in a good, cold freezer.
Q: Is your beef and lamb 100% grass-fed and grass-finished?
Yes. Our Angus cattle and Katahdin sheep are 100% grass-fed and grass-finished.They are raised on pasture and forage throughout their lives and are never grain-finished.During different seasons, their forage may include native grasses, improved pastures, seasonal cover forage, natural browse, and hay grown on our farm.
Q: Are your animals born and raised on your farm?
Yes. We are a true pasture-to-plate family farm.The beef and lamb we market come from animals that are born and raised on our farm.Knowing where our animals come from allows us to manage their care, nutrition, handling, and environment from birth through harvest.
Q: Do you use hormones or antibiotics?
Our market cattle and sheep are raised without added growth hormones or routine antibiotics.Animal welfare always comes first. If an animal requires medical treatment, we provide the care it needs and that animal is removed from the certified market program.Our focus is on good animal husbandry, quality forage, rotational grazing, clean water, proper nutrition, and preventative management.
Q: What certifications does Sampson Family Farm have?
Our beef and lamb are Certified Grassfed by A Greener World.Our farm is Certified Animal Welfare Approved by A Greener World.We are also certified through the American Grassfed Association.These independent certification programs provide standards and outside verification of our grass-fed production methods, animal-welfare practices, and farm management.Certification is important to us because it gives our customers more than simply our word about how their food is raised.
Q: What does Certified Grassfed mean?
Certified Grassfed means our cattle and sheep are raised on a grass- and forage-based diet rather than being grain-finished.Our livestock spend their lives on pasture where they can graze naturally.During times when fresh forage is limited, such as winter or drought conditions, we supplement with approved forage and hay.Our farm is audited annually to be sure we are following the highest grassfed and finished standards.
Q: What does Animal Welfare Approved mean?
Animal Welfare Approved is an independent certification program with standards covering the care and management of livestock.The standards address areas such as access to pasture, animal handling, health management, living conditions, transportation, and other practices related to animal welfare.We also select processors that meet the animal-welfare requirements associated with our certification program.
Q: What is the difference between USDA-inspected meat and custom-exempt beef?
We offer meat through two different processing methods.USDA-inspected beef and lamb can be sold as individual cuts. This is the meat you will find in our online store and at our farmers' market and Meat Up locations.With custom-exempt bulk purchases, the customer purchases ownership of the animal or their portion of the animal before processing. The processor then processes that animal for the owner's personal use. Custom-exempt packages are marked "Not for Sale" and cannot be resold to other parties.This allows customers to purchase beef in larger quantities such as an Eighth, Quarter, Half, or Whole animal at a lower processing cost.
Q: What is the difference between live weight, hanging weight, and packaged weight?
These three weights are different and understanding them makes purchasing bulk beef much easier.Live weight is the weight of the animal before harvest.Hanging weight is the weight of the carcass after harvest and initial processing, before it is cut into individual packages.Packaged or freezer weight is the amount of finished meat you take home after aging, trimming, boning, cutting, and packaging.The packaged weight will always be less than the hanging weight, and the hanging weight will be considerably less than the live weight.
Q: How is the price of my bulk beef calculated?
Pricing depends on the size of beef share your purchase.For Whole and Half Beef, the farm portion of the price is based on the animal's certified live weight after harvest. Processing charges are paid separately to the processor and are generally based on hanging weight and processing services.Quarter and Eighth Beef are offered as predetermined packages with processing included in the stated package price.Because animals naturally vary in size, final weights and costs can vary. Current pricing and estimated take-home weights are listed on our Bulk Beef page.
Q: Do I pay Sampson Family Farm and the processor separately?
For a Whole or Half Beef, you will receive a farm invoice from Sampson Family Farm and a separate processing invoice from the processor.For our Quarter and Eighth Beef packages, processing is included in the package price and handled by the farm.A deposit is required when you reserve your beef.Final payment arrangements will be explained when your animal is scheduled for harvest.
Q: What is a split Quarter Beef?
A Quarter Beef is not simply the front quarter or hind quarter of an animal.Our quarters are split halves, which means each Quarter Beef receives a balanced selection of meat from both the front and rear portions of the animal.This allows each customer to receive a variety of steaks, roasts, ground beef, stew meat, and other cuts rather than receiving only the cuts found in one section of the animal.
Q: Can I choose how my beef is cut?
Customers purchasing a Whole or Half Beef have the opportunity to speak with the processor and customize their cutting instructions.You can discuss steak thickness, number of steaks per package, roast sizes, ground beef, and other available processing options directly with the processor.Quarter and Eighth Beef are packaged using our standard cut selection so that each customer receives a balanced assortment of cuts.
Q: Can I request organ meats, bones, or other specialty cuts?
Customers purchasing a Whole or Half Beef can discuss available organ meats and specialty items with the processor when completing their cutting instructions.Depending on availability and the animal, these may include items such as liver, heart, tongue, soup bones, or other specialty cuts.We also periodically have USDA-inspected organ meats, bones, and specialty products available through our individual-cut inventory.
Q: Why can my harvest date change?
Our harvest dates are scheduled based on when we expect an animal to be properly finished, but farming does not always follow an exact calendar.Because our cattle are grass-fed and grass-finished, weather, rainfall, heat, pasture conditions, and forage quality can affect how quickly an animal reaches the proper finish.We would rather allow an animal the additional time it needs than harvest simply because a date is on the calendar.Processor schedules can also occasionally affect harvest dates. If there is a change to your scheduled animal, we will contact you.
Q: How will I know when my beef or lamb is ready?
We stay in contact with you throughout the process.After you place your deposit, your order is reserved for an upcoming harvest. As the harvest date approaches, we will provide the information you need regarding processing, cutting instructions when applicable, final payment, and pickup.Once processing is complete, arrangements will be made for you to receive your order.
Q: How is my meat packaged?
Our beef and lamb are professionally cut and packaged by the processor and frozen for safe transportation and storage.Package sizes vary depending on the cut and your processing instructions. Ground beef is generally packaged in convenient family-sized portions, while steaks, roasts, and other cuts are packaged according to the processor's specifications or your custom instructions when available.
Q: Do you sell individual cuts if I don't need a Quarter or Half?
Yes. You do not have to purchase bulk beef or lamb to buy from Sampson Family Farm.We offer USDA-inspected individual cuts of beef and lamb, including a rotating selection of ground meat, steaks, roasts, stew meat, organ meats, bones, sausage, and other products.Availability changes throughout the year, so check our online store for current inventory.
Q: What is a Meat Up?
Our Meat Ups are scheduled pickup locations that allow customers in other areas of Florida to purchase from our farm without having to drive all the way to Live Oak.Customers place their orders ahead of time, and we bring the completed orders to the scheduled Meat Up location.Current dates and locations are posted on our website and social media.
Q: Can I come to the farm anytime to purchase meat?
Sampson Family Farm is a working family farm and our home, rather than a traditional retail storefront.Farm pickups and visits are by appointment so we can make sure someone is available to help you.For customers who prefer regular shopping hours, you can also find us at the Alachua County Farmers Market or use one of our scheduled Meat Up locations.
Q: How far in advance should I reserve bulk beef or lamb?
We recommend reserving as early as possible.Our animals are raised and finished naturally on pasture, so we only have a certain number available for each harvest period. Bulk orders are reserved with a deposit, and availability can fill before a scheduled harvest date.If the date you want is full, we can usually place you on the next available harvest.
Q: Is grass-fed beef different from conventional beef?
Yes. Grass-fed and grass-finished beef is produced differently from cattle finished on grain.Our cattle spend their lives eating grass and forage, which generally produces beef that is leaner than heavily grain-finished beef while still providing the natural flavor and tenderness we select for in our Angus cattle.Because grass-fed beef can be leaner, it often cooks more quickly than conventional beef.
Q: How should I cook grass-fed beef?
Grass-fed beef generally benefits from slightly lower cooking temperatures and careful attention to cooking time.For steaks, avoid overcooking and allow the meat to rest after cooking. Slow-cooking methods work very well for roasts, brisket, and other cuts that contain more connective tissue.One of the advantages of purchasing bulk beef is receiving a variety of cuts, and we are always happy to help customers learn how to use cuts they may not have cooked before.

It is often used for dishes like pot roast, beef stew, or as thin-sliced roast beef for sandwiches.

Grass-Fed Tallow Products

From our Pastures to your Counter

Our tallow products begin with suet from cattle raised right here on Sampson Family Farm. Suet is the firm, clean fat found around the kidneys and loins of cattle. It differs from ordinary meat-trimming fat and is especially valued for producing smooth, high-quality tallow when carefully rendered.

Because our cattle are grass-fed and grass-finished, we know exactly where our tallow comes from and how the animals were raised. The rendered tallow is combined with thoughtfully selected organic ingredients to create simple, naturally made products for you.

By using the suet from our cattle, we honor the whole animal and turn a valuable farm resource into useful products for your family.

Farm raised. Naturally made. From our family farm to yours.
